data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's claim that the program: forbidden case must mutate the synchronous precondition to an asynchronous post-provider-call check conflates an implementation-ordering mutation with the problem's actual behavioral standard. The problem demands that the lease-mismatch refusal be returned before any provider call; a suite that stubs the provider and asserts it was never invoked already guards that temporal invariant. SRC_001 does not establish a causal mechanism by which re-ordering the check to post-call would *silently pass* such an invocation-count assertion: if the stub records any provider call, the suite fails immediately. The proposed mutation is therefore redundant against the existing temporal guard rather than naming a distinct silent-pass mutation that the suite would today miss.
